I've been farming this land for 50 years. I know this soil. I know what works. My father farmed before me, and I've watched the seasons long enough that I don't need anyone to tell me what to do.

My 14.5 mu grows wheat in the winter and maize in the summer — same land, both seasons, the way it's always been done here in Quzhou. My wife and I manage it ourselves. We don't need hired hands for a farm this size.

For the **wheat**, I'll plant in October like every year. I buy my seeds from the county seed shop — the same improved variety I've used the past several years, Jimai 22 or whatever the shop has that's similar. It yields well and I know how it behaves. I'll do rotary tillage before planting — it's easier on my back than deep ploughing and the soil here doesn't need turning over every year. I'll put down base fertilizer before sowing — diammonium phosphate for phosphorus and potassium, urea for nitrogen — then topdress nitrogen again at jointing. I'll irrigate four times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading, and once during grain filling. I'll spray herbicide in late autumn and fungicide once or twice in spring for rust and powdery mildew. I expect about 450 jin per mu — maybe more if the rains cooperate.

For the **maize**, after wheat harvest in June, I'll plant right away. I've used Zhengdan 958 for years. It's reliable. I won't plough — just rotary till the stubble and plant. Same fertilizer approach: base application plus topdress at big bell stage. Maize here doesn't need as much water as wheat, but I'll irrigate three times — at seedling if it's dry, at big bell, and at silking. I'll spray once for corn borer and check for fall armyworm since it's been showing up more lately. I expect around 550 jin per mu.

Two people, 14.5 mu, two crops — this is what I know how to do.
